summary: The incident is real, localized to auth-service's token-validation path, and per the reviewed analysis the root cause is NOT adequately established: H1 (JWT library/TokenValidator regression from dep-5710) at 0.45 and H2 (scheduled signing-key rotation cfg-2705 published before all validators adopted it) at 0.40 remain effectively tied and name different origins and fixes. What is solid: a single-minute step in auth-service error_rate from ~0.2% to ~36% at 2026-04-15T14:02:00Z with flat throughput (~400 req/s) and p99 (~90 ms), a flat ~2h plateau (latest 15:56Z), and an independent, time-aligned ~21% error plateau at the unchanged caller api-gateway, which rules out a log-pipeline reporting artifact (H5). Fleet-wide sweeps show the only changes all day are auth-service dep-5710 v7.3.0 at 14:00Z ('jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)', 'TokenValidator rewritten') and cfg-2705 at 14:01Z (jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04); both are still live and neither was ever reverted. Every decisive discriminator is unreachable in this run: no per-instance/pod, endpoint or token-issuer dimension exists, no diff/JWKS-source/rotation-mode metadata exists, the deployed library version is self-contradictory, and the single-change rollback test could not be run with read-only tooling (logs also unsearchable). H3 (clock skew/cert) and H4's resource-exhaustion arm are not supported; H4's pod-restart arm is not closed out. Immediate action is a safe mitigation plus the rollback experiment: roll back dep-5710 first (H1 is the marginally better fit on shape), then re-test with cfg-2705 reverted if the error persists.

ranked_hypotheses.title: JWT library upgrade (dep-5710) introduced a token-validation regression
ranked_hypotheses.statement: auth-service deploy dep-5710 v7.3.0 at 14:00:00Z replaced the JWT parser (jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12, described as a breaking parser API change) and rewrote TokenValidator. The new/unmigrated validation path emits a wrong invalid_token verdict for a persistent subset of otherwise-valid tokens, producing a step from ~0.2% to ~36% error_rate at 14:02:00Z that plateaus for ~2h without converging, with throughput and p99 latency untouched. The deterministic, converging-never nature of the plateau fits a code fault better than a propagation race. NOTE the mechanism hop remains unevidenced: no diff, no clock-skew/TTL/strictness defaults, and the deployed library version is self-contradictory, so this is a timing-and-shape argument, not a mechanism proof.

causal_chain.claim: Deploy dep-5710 v7.3.0 goes live at 14:00:00Z as the only fleet deployment that day, with a breaking jjwt parser API change and a rewritten TokenValidator; never rolled back.
The rewritten validator applies different parser semantics (clock-skew default / claim strictness) to a class of valid tokens, inverting them to invalid_token.
auth-service error_rate steps from 0.16% (14:01Z) to 36.08% (14:02Z), exactly 2 minutes after the deploy, then holds 35-39% through 15:59Z with no decay.
The fault is a wrong-verdict, not load or resource: throughput flat ~390-417 req/s, p99 flat ~86-95 ms, cpu_pct ~38%, memory_pct ~52%, rate_limited ~2/min.
api-gateway, the caller of auth-service, shows an independent contemporaneous ~21% error plateau in the same window, confirming a real user-facing fault rather than a reporting artifact.

assumptions: The deployed jjwt version is unknown (F33: summary says '4.x', change list says '0.12'); the hypothesis only requires that parser semantics changed materially, which both strings assert.
The TokenValidator rewrite's behavioural delta is unknown (F34: one-line string only); the 'inverts a class of valid tokens' hop is assumed, not evidenced.
Because no instance/endpoint/issuer label exists (F26), the ~36% is treated as uniform across the service aggregate; a per-instance split cannot be measured and is not claimed as support.
No unlogged change on an implicit dependency (secrets manager / mesh / JWKS) occurred; F19/F20/F41/F44 show no recorded one, but the change feed is service-scoped only.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Scheduled signing-key rotation (cfg-2705) published a new key_id before all validators/consumers adopted it
ranked_hypotheses.statement: security-automation rotated jwt.signing.key_id from 'k-2025-10' to 'k-2026-04' at 14:01:00Z as a single un-staged key assignment on auth-service. A fraction of token validations then resolve the wrong key (or a validator holds/expects the previous key_id), yielding invalid_token for ~1/3 of validations, one minute before the 14:02:00Z error step. This matches the HIST-108 precedent (lead only). The hypothesis carries an unresolved internal weakness: a key-propagation race should converge as validators reload, yet the error is a flat 35-39% plateau for ~2h with no decay, which requires an unobserved permanently-stalled (or per-pod-frozen) reload.
ranked_hypotheses.root_cause_service: auth-service signing-key configuration / key distribution path

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2705, the only config change fleet-wide on 2026-04-15, rotates jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04 on auth-service at 14:01:00Z; single key-value assignment with no dual-key/grace/overlap field; never reverted.
The new key_id is live before every validator/consumer has adopted it (or a subset keeps using the old key_id), so those validations resolve the wrong key and return invalid_token.
If the keys are resolved per-pod (HIST-108-style JWKS reload), only lagging pods would fail - but the plateau is flat, so any such partition must be frozen for ~2h.
auth-service error_rate steps to ~36% at 14:02:00Z, 1 minute after the rotation, with unchanged throughput/latency/resources, and holds through 15:59Z.
api-gateway, the caller, inherits a contemporaneous ~21% error plateau.

assumptions: The rotation was not staged/dual-key: F35 shows no grace/overlap field, but F35/F43/F47 concede the record is silent in both directions, so 'single hard cutover' is NOT established.
Whether auth-service reads the key from one shared source or per-pod JWKS is unknown (F43/F45/F47); the mechanism requires per-pod or partially-updated resolution, which no source confirms.

The ~36% cut is defined by key_id/issuance epoch relative to 14:01:00Z; this is unmeasured - F26 shows only a fleet-aggregate series with no issuer/key/instance dimension, so '~1/3 of tokens' is an inference from one number.
An unobserved mechanism keeps a propagation race permanently non-convergent (no finding supports a stalled reload).
HIST-108 is a lead only (F46): its one-line resolution does not establish the key-loading model for this incident.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bad/partial auth-service pod subset (crash-looping or hung instances) fails a fraction of calls
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A subset of auth-service instances is unhealthy - crash-looping, hung, or not fully rolled out - so a fraction of requests land on an instance that returns 401/errors while healthy instances serve the rest. NOT closed out: F26 shows no instance/pod dimension exists, so a uniform-vs-split partition cannot be measured, and F31 + the tool log show the 'restarts' metric and the auth-service ERROR log query both failed with backend 503, so restart counts are unknown.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5710 rolls out at 14:00:00Z as a single whole-service event with no canary/stage/rollout-percentage metadata and no rollback.
A subset of instances is unhealthy (crash-loop/hung/unmigrated) and returns errors for the traffic it serves.
Service-level CPU (~38%) and memory (~52%) are flat across onset, arguing against resource pressure or OOM-driven restarts at the aggregate level.
Restart counts and pod-level state are UNKNOWN because the 'restarts' metric query returned 503 and no instance label exists, so a crash-looping subset is not excluded.
api-gateway sees a contemporaneous elevated error plateau, consistent with a fraction of auth calls failing.

assumptions: The failing instances return 401/5xx without adding p99 latency or reducing throughput - hard to reconcile with a crash loop, which is why this stays low-probability.
Per-instance error data would be needed to confirm; F26 shows such a dimension does not exist in this backend, making this hypothesis close to unfalsifiable rather than merely untested.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Clock skew / NTP drift or expired certificate makes a fraction of tokens appear expired/unverifiable
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A clock source drifted or a certificate in the validation path expired, so a subset of token validations fail on expiry/verification checks independent of the two auth-service changes.
ranked_hypotheses.root_cause_service: auth-service hosts / platform clock (NTP) or TLS certificate in the validation path

causal_chain.claim: A time source or certificate degrades so a fraction of tokens appear expired or unverifiable.
auth-service error_rate steps to ~36% at 14:02:00Z and plateaus to 15:59Z.
api-gateway inherits elevated errors in the same window.

assumptions: A clock/cert fault would coincidentally produce a clean single-minute step at 14:02:00Z, 1-2 minutes after the only two fleet changes of the day (implausible).
No change or telemetry record for a clock/cert fault exists anywhere in the window (F19, F20, F41, F44).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Reporter's framing: the 36% error rate is partly an artifact of the identity-namespace log-pipeline outage
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The down log pipeline in the identity namespace distorted error reporting or traffic accounting, so the measured 36% 401 rate overstates or mis-attributes the real user-facing impact. Rejected: the decisive counter-evidence is NOT metric self-consistency (the same backend returned 503s and has no instance dimension) but the INDEPENDENT caller-side series: api-gateway, which had zero deployments and zero config changes all day, shows its own ~21% error plateau starting in the same 13:54-14:03Z bucket. A log-pipeline artifact in the identity namespace cannot manufacture a synchronized error step in an unchanged, independently-instrumented caller.

causal_chain.claim: identity-namespace log pipeline down since morning, so auth-service logs are unsearchable and log queries return 503.
The reported 36% and api-gateway's ~21% both derive from the same metric backend.
Independent caller-side evidence falsifies the artifact reading: api-gateway was unchanged all day (zero deploys, zero config changes) yet shows a contemporaneous ~21% error plateau.

assumptions: None material; the only residual is that the metric backend itself could be globally wrong, which would still not explain api-gateway's independent plateau being time-aligned with auth-service's.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Falsified by the independent caller-side series: api-gateway had zero deployments and zero config changes on 2026-04-15 (F5) yet shows its own ~21% error plateau in the same 13:54-14:03Z bucket as auth-service's step (F11). Throughput (F9) and latency are unchanged, so there is no traffic-accounting distortion. This is a genuine, caller-observable fault, not a log-pipeline reporting artifact.

facts.statement: auth-service error_rate stepped from a ~0.2% baseline to ~36% in a single minute at 2026-04-15T14:02:00Z (14:00=0.26%, 14:01=0.16%, 14:02=36.08%, 14:03=38.34%).
The elevated error rate is a persistent, flat plateau ~35-39% from 14:02Z through the latest data (15:56Z, last 36.53%, max 40.33% at 15:08Z), with no decay and no second step.
auth-service throughput is unaffected across onset: request_rate stays ~390-417 req/s before and after (13:56=390.51, 14:00=400.07, 14:04=404.31, 15:56=408.9).
auth-service latency_p99_ms shows no change at onset, steady ~86-95 ms across 13:50-14:12.

api-gateway, a caller of auth-service, shows a contemporaneous elevated error_rate plateau of ~21% (13:54 bucket avg=2.51 max=20.72, 14:03=21.21, sustained ~20.7-21.4% through 15:51), with onset in the same 13:54-14:03Z bucket as auth-service.
api-gateway had zero deployments and zero config changes between 00:00Z and 15:59Z on 2026-04-15.

The only deployment anywhere in the fleet in the window is auth-service dep-5710 v7.3.0 at 2026-04-15T14:00:00Z, summarised as 'Upgrade JWT library to 4.x; refactor token validation' with changes 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)' and 'TokenValidator rewritten'; status 'live', rolled_back_at null.

The only config change in the window is auth-service cfg-2705: jwt.signing.key_id rotated from 'k-2025-10' to 'k-2026-04' at 2026-04-15T14:01:00Z by author 'security-automation', description 'Scheduled signing-key rotation'; it was not reverted.

The deploy's metadata is internally contradictory about the JWT library version (summary 'JWT library to 4.x' vs change list 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12'); no version, dependency lock or diff is present, so the deployed jjwt version is not resolvable.
The TokenValidator rewrite is captured only as the one-line string 'TokenValidator rewritten'; no diff, config values, or clock-skew/TTL/claim-strictness defaults are exposed.
cfg-2705 is recorded as a single key-value assignment with no second key entry, no 'previous key retained', no overlap/grace-period field, and no reload/JWKS-source setting.

No source (cfg-2705 record, the config store service-scoped 2025-01-01 to 2026-04-15 or fleet-wide 2025-10-01 to 2026-04-15, or the dependency graph) exposes auth-service's key-loading topology (shared single source vs per-pod JWKS).

The dependency graph contains no key-store/JWKS, secrets-manager, config-service or service-mesh node; auth-service's downstream nodes are only user-db (postgres), redis-cache (redis, shared) and kyc-provider (external, has_telemetry=false).

redis-cache is the single SHARED component in auth-service's neighbourhood (also used by portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service); a redis-cache-scoped config-change query for 13:30-15:59Z returned count=0.
auth-service resource metrics are flat across onset: cpu_pct ~37-39% and memory_pct ~50-53%, with no step at 14:02 or ramp.
auth-service rate_limited_per_min is flat and low across the window (2.15 at 13:50, 2.33 at 14:02, 2.1 at 15:56; mean 2.02), so no throttling surge accompanies the step.
auth-service's available_metrics expose no instance/pod, endpoint or token-issuer dimension; every query returns a single fleet-aggregate series.

The restart metric query ('restart_count') failed as not_found and the follow-up 'restarts' query and the auth-service ERROR log query both failed with backend unavailable (503); restart counts and a log-based 401 breakdown were not obtained.

Neither change was ever reverted: dep-5710 is still status 'live' with rolled_back_at null as of 15:59Z, and no k-2026-04 -> k-2025-10 revert record exists, so no post-revert error_rate series exists in the window and the single-change rollback experiment was not run.

Historical precedents are leads only: HIST-108 (2025-10-01) '401s after JWT signing key rotation', root cause 'Key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS', resolved by re-publishing the previous key and staging the rotation; HIST-109 (2025-07-11) 'Token validation regression after auth library upgrade', root cause 'JWT library upgrade changed clock-skew default', resolved by rollback/pinning skew.
HIST-108's resolution text is a one-liner that does not state the key-loading model or whether the rotation was a hard swap, so it is consistent with either per-pod JWKS or a staged shared rotation.

Only one deployment and one config change occurred during the incident window; the sole other fleet deployment all day was market-data-service dep-5699 v5.0.3 at 11:35Z ('Fix symbol mapping'), outside the identity path.

assumptions: The deployed jjwt version is unknown (F33: summary says '4.x', change list says '0.12'); H1 only requires that parser semantics changed materially, which both strings assert.
The TokenValidator rewrite's behavioural delta is unknown (F34: one-line string only); the 'inverts a class of valid tokens' hop is assumed, not evidenced.

Because no instance/endpoint/issuer label exists (F26), the ~36% is treated as a uniform service aggregate; the '~1/3 of tokens fail' framing is an inference from one number and is not used as evidence for either H1 or H2.

Whether auth-service reads the signing key from one shared source or per-pod JWKS is unknown (F43/F45/F47), so H2's required propagation mechanism can be neither confirmed nor excluded; 'single hard cutover' is not established.
An unobserved mechanism would be needed to keep a key-propagation race permanently non-convergent; no finding supports a stalled or frozen reload.
No unlogged change on an implicit dependency (secrets manager / service mesh / JWKS) occurred; F19/F20/F41/F44/F48 show no recorded one, but the change feed is service-scoped only.
HIST-108 and HIST-109 are leads only and do not establish the key-loading model or the parser semantics for this incident.
'Healthy metrics' claims rest on single series from a backend that returned 503s for some queries, so they should be read as 'no evidence of a load/resource cause' rather than 'excluded'.
The reported symptoms (401 invalid_token at 36%) accurately describe the fault; the error string itself could not be confirmed from logs.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) Ordering against the confirmed onset: deploy 14:00:00Z then key rotation 14:01:00Z then error step at 14:02:00Z, leaving a 1-2 minute gap between each change and the step; both changes are plausible causal candidates.

timeline.event: Start of the day-wide change sweep window; fleet-wide config query for 00:00-15:59Z returns exactly one record (cfg-2705), i.e. no second credential/secret change anywhere before onset.
Only other fleet deployment all day: market-data-service dep-5699 v5.0.3 ('Fix symbol mapping'), outside the identity path.
Steady-state baseline: auth-service error_rate ~0.2%, request_rate ~390-417 req/s, p99 ~86-95 ms, cpu ~38%, memory ~51%, rate_limited ~2/min.
api-gateway error_rate begins rising (13:54 bucket avg=2.51, max=20.72), the same broad bucket as auth-service's later step.

auth-service dep-5710 v7.3.0 goes live ('Upgrade JWT library to 4.x; refactor token validation'; changes 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)' and 'TokenValidator rewritten'), status 'live', no canary/rollout metadata, never rolled back.
cfg-2705 by 'security-automation' rotates jwt.signing.key_id from 'k-2025-10' to 'k-2026-04'; recorded as a single un-staged assignment with no grace/overlap or reload/JWKS-source field.
auth-service error_rate steps from 0.16% (14:01) to 36.08% (14:02), reaching 38.34% at 14:03, with throughput, p99 latency, cpu, memory and rate-limit all unchanged.
api-gateway error_rate plateau confirmed at ~21% (14:03=21.21, sustained ~20.7-21.4% through 15:51) despite zero api-gateway deployments or config changes all day.
Incident INC-007 reported (SEV-1): users logged out / 401 invalid_token on ~1/3 of validations; identity-namespace log pipeline already down, so auth-service logs unsearchable.
Maximum observed error_rate in the plateau: 40.33%.
Latest auth-service data: error_rate still 36.53%, request_rate 408.9 req/s - a flat ~2h plateau with no decay or recovery.

Decisive re-checks: dep-5710 still 'live' with rolled_back_at null and no revert of cfg-2705 anywhere in the fleet; no post-revert error series exists, so the single-change rollback test remains untested.

recommended_actions.action: Immediate mitigation (safe, change-free): if a partial mitigation is needed while tests run, keep dep-5710 live as-is and page the auth-service on-call to prepare the rollback; do NOT make any additional auth-service config change, since adding a second change now would destroy the ability to attribute the fault.
recommended_actions.rationale: Both candidate changes are still live and unattributed (F38, F39); a third change would confound the only remaining discriminator and, with auth-service logs unsearchable (F31), there is no way to trace it afterward.

recommended_actions.action: Immediate discriminating test #1 (the single decisive runnable test): roll back ONLY dep-5710 (auth-service, revert to the pre-7.3.0 build, previously live at 14:00:00Z) and watch auth-service error_rate for 10-15 minutes. If the ~36% plateau collapses toward the ~0.2% baseline, H1 is the root cause.
recommended_actions.rationale: H1 is the marginally better fit on shape - a flat, non-converging ~2h plateau with flat throughput/latency fits a deterministic code-level validation fault better than a propagation race that should converge (F8, F17, F28). Neither change has ever been reverted, so this test has never been run and no post-revert error series exists (F38, F40, F42).

recommended_actions.action: Immediate discriminating test #2 (only if error_rate does NOT recover after reverting dep-5710): revert cfg-2705 by re-publishing jwt.signing.key_id 'k-2025-10' (and re-publishing the previous signing key so all validators can load it) and watch auth-service error_rate for 10-15 minutes. Recovery here confirms H2.
recommended_actions.rationale: No revert/re-publish of jwt.signing.key_id exists anywhere in the fleet and no graceful overlap or previous-key retention is recorded (F35, F39, F41, F43), so the HIST-108 failure mode (new key_id published before all pods loaded the JWKS) is untested for this incident (F6, F46, F47).

recommended_actions.action: Immediate instrumentation to make the tests conclusive: capture auth-service error/401 counts and restart counts during and after each rollback (retry the 'restarts' metric and the auth-service ERROR log query when the backend is available), and separately restore/reroute the identity-namespace log pipeline (the pre-existing separate ticket) so the 401 verdict text can be read.
recommended_actions.rationale: The 'restarts' metric and the auth-service ERROR log query both failed with 503, so restart counts and the exact 401 error string were never obtained (F31); logs are the cheapest way to see whether failures say 'unknown key' (H2) versus expiry/claim-parse (H1).

recommended_actions.action: Short-term: once the offending change is identified and reverted, run a staged, single-variable re-application - deploy the TokenValidator/jjwt change alone (with a pinned, explicit library version and recorded clock-skew/TTL/claim-strictness defaults) and then the key rotation alone as a dual-key/staged rotation with the previous key retained - and verify error_rate stays at baseline after each step.
recommended_actions.rationale: The deploy metadata contradicts itself on the library version and exposes no diff or defaults (F33, F34), and cfg-2705 has no overlap/grace/previous-key field (F35), so neither change can currently be re-applied safely. This also supplies the per-change attribution that the metric backend cannot (F26).

recommended_actions.action: Short-term: add per-instance/pod, per-endpoint and per-token-issuer label dimensions to auth-service metrics, and add a deployment canary/rollout-percentage and rollback field, so a uniform-vs-split error partition is measurable in future.
recommended_actions.rationale: The metric backend exposes only fleet-aggregate series with no instance, endpoint or issuer dimension (F26), so the H1-predicts-uniform vs H2-predicts-per-key-epoch-split test cannot be run at all; deployment records also lack canary/rollout granularity (F32).

recommended_actions.action: Long-term: make signing-key rotation staged and dual-key by default, with rotation mode, JWKS source and previous-key retention recorded explicitly in the config/change metadata, and make the key-loading topology visible as a first-class dependency node.
recommended_actions.rationale: No source anywhere - cfg-2705's record, the service-scoped and fleet-wide config store, or the dependency graph - exposes whether the key comes from a shared source or per-pod JWKS, and there is no key-store/JWKS/mesh node in the graph (F35, F43, F44, F45, F47). HIST-108 (F46) shows this ambiguity has already caused one incident.

recommended_actions.action: Long-term: gate JWT-parser/validator upgrades behind a canary with a mandatory recorded dependency lock and diff link, and add an automated post-deploy check that asserts the invalid_token verdict rate, so a parser-semantics change cannot silently invert a token class.
recommended_actions.rationale: The TokenValidator change is evidenced only by two one-line strings with a self-contradictory library version (F16, F33, F34), and the resulting 36% wrong-verdict rate ran ~2h with no rollback (F8, F38) - exactly the HIST-109 failure mode (F6).

recommended_actions.action: Long-term: close the observability gap that blocked this investigation - restore and monitor the identity-namespace log pipeline, and add a redundancy/fallback path so a single metric-backend 503 cannot blind an incident.
recommended_actions.rationale: The identity-namespace log pipeline was already down at report time and the metric backend returned 503 for the 'restarts' query and the auth-service ERROR log query (F31), preventing log-based attribution between the two candidate changes.

data_gaps: auth-service logs are unsearchable (identity-namespace log pipeline down since the morning), so the 401 verdicts could not be traced to a failing key/credential lookup or to a claim/clock check - this is the single most useful missing artifact for separating H2 from H1.

The metric backend exposes no instance/pod, endpoint or token-issuer label dimension (F26), so the uniform-vs-split partition (H1 predicts uniform; H2 predicts a split by key epoch or by reloaded pods) cannot be measured at all - the decisive test is unreachable rather than merely unrequested.

No metadata source exposes the TokenValidator diff, commit/PR body, dependency lock or genuine jjwt version (F33 self-contradictory), nor its clock-skew/TTL/claim-strictness defaults (F34), so H1's mechanism hop cannot be confirmed or refuted.

No source exposes whether auth-service resolves the signing key from one shared source or per-pod JWKS, nor whether cfg-2705 retained the previous key or was a hard cutover (F35, F43, F44, F45, F47) - so H2's mechanism cannot be confirmed or excluded.

The single-change rollback experiment (revert cfg-2705 only, or roll back dep-5710 only) was never run and is not runnable with the read-only tooling; neither change was ever reverted (F38-F42), so the discriminating post-revert error series does not exist.

auth-service restart counts are unknown: the 'restart_count' query failed as not_found and the 'restarts' query failed with 503 (F31), so H4's pod-restart arm is NOT closed out; flat cpu/memory (F29) argues against resource pressure but not against a crash-looping subset.

The ~36% figure is a fleet-aggregate with no issuer/instance dimension (F26), so the '~1/3 of tokens fail' framing is an inference from one number, not a measured partition, and cannot be used to favor H1 over H2.

The change feed is service-scoped only and contains no secrets-manager, config-service or service-mesh node (F24, F45); an unlogged/out-of-band credential or policy change is therefore unobservable, though no such change was recorded for 00:00-15:59Z (F19, F20, F41, F44).
A fleet-wide config query for 2026-03-01 to 2026-04-15 failed twice with 503 (F48), so only a single wide 2025-10-01 to 2026-04-15 window corroborates the count=1 result (F44).

Upstream callers other than api-gateway (order-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service, payment-service, settlement-service, exchange-gateway, notification-service) were not individually checked for elevated error_rate, so the full blast radius is unconfirmed beyond api-gateway's ~21% plateau (F11, F12).
redis-cache runtime telemetry (hit/miss, eviction, failover, replica sync) was not queried; only the absence of a recorded redis-cache config/deploy change is established (F21, F23).
'Healthy metrics' claims rest on single aggregate series from a backend that returned 503s on several queries (F29, F31), so resource causes are not excluded, only unsupported.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Reverting dep-5710 alone and observing auth-service error_rate fall from ~36% back toward the ~0.2% baseline within minutes would establish H1 as the root cause and overturn the inconclusive outcome.
Reverting cfg-2705 (re-publishing key 'k-2025-10' and the previous signing key) with error_rate recovery while dep-5710 stays live would establish H2 as the root cause.

A per-instance/per-pod error breakdown showing failures concentrated in ~1/3 of instances (rather than uniform across the fleet aggregate) would favor H2's propagation mechanism over H1's deterministic code fault.
A per-token-issuer or issuance-epoch breakdown showing failures clustered around the 14:01Z key rotation would favor H2; a break confined to a token class independent of issuance time would favor H1.

Log evidence showing 'unknown key'/'signature verification failed' style verdicts would favor H2, whereas 'expired'/'claim parse' verdicts would favor H1 - currently unobtainable because the auth-service log query returns 503.

Evidence of a deliberately stalled or permanently frozen key reload (or a JWKS source shared by all pods, which would make a partial-propagation race impossible) would decisively move the ranking between H2 and H1.

Recovery of dep-5710's diff or dependency lock showing no semantic change to clock-skew/TTL/claim-strictness would weaken H1; showing a changed clock-skew or strictness default would strongly support H1 (the HIST-109 mechanism).

A discovered unlogged change on an implicit dependency (secrets manager, service mesh/policy, or JWKS endpoint) contemporaneous with 14:01-14:02Z would introduce a third candidate and invalidate the two-change attribution.

Evidence that the 14:02Z step is an artifact of the metric backend itself (e.g. a known backend-wide miscalculation spanning the window) would undercut the localization, though it would still have to explain api-gateway's independent ~21% plateau.
Per-instance restart data showing a crash-looping or hung pod subset would revive H4, especially if the failing instances also account for the ~36% share of traffic.

H2 also cannot be demoted on the grounds that the key source is shared, since no field asserts that either. If anything, HIST-108 is the only adjacent datapoint and its root cause is explicitly a per-pod JWKS propagation failure.
